Thanks for the clear repro, Alicia — sorry about the friction. Quick questions so we can triage:

1) Which browser versions did you test (Chrome/Edge exact versions)?
2) Can you reproduce in an incognito/private window?
3) If possible, please capture a HAR or the network console. If not, a short screen recording will do.

Two immediate checks on our side: we suspect a cookie / SameSite handling issue on the /accept flow that can cause the OTP check to lose session state and reload the form. Ben — I’m looping you in to look at recent deploys to the Zip adapter and any cookie changes in the last 24h.

Alicia — as a short-term workaround, if your user can try:
- Incognito window (Chrome) and copy/paste the invite URL; or
- Use a different device (personal phone) to accept the invite; or
- If the portal shows an option to "Resend invite via email" that sometimes bypasses the redirect.

We’ll follow up within the hour with a concrete fix or a ticket.

— David

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Trouble accepting Zip invite — initial triage notes

Forwarding Alicia's report — copied below. Quick interim findings from a quick log sweep:

- Observed several 302s returning to /invite/accept when the OTP POST hits the /session/validate endpoint. The session cookie for the invite host (invite.zip.vendor-portal.com) is being set without SameSite=None; for modern browsers that can drop the cookie on cross-site navigations.
- There was a small change yesterday to the cookie defaults in the Zip adapter where we attempted to upgrade a cookie to Lax in an effort to reduce CSRF noise. That could explain timing.

Suggested immediate actions:
1) Ops: roll a targeted config override to set the invite cookie to SameSite=None; Secure for the /accept path. That will prevent the browser from omitting the cookie on the OTP redirect. (This is low-risk and reversible.)
2) Engineering: add a short server-side fallback so OTP validation tolerates a missing session cookie when a valid one-time code and fingerprint header are present.
3) Support: reply to the customer with a step-by-step workaround (incognito + clear cookies) while we push the config.

I filed SUP ticket JIRA-SUP-5471 and attached a small HAR from our test machine (network-harvest.log). I'll push a config override to staging now and monitor.

Ben Carter
Senior Infra Engineer — Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia — thanks for the report and patience. We deployed a targeted config override to the invite host to set the invite cookie to SameSite=None; Secure and monitored for 30 minutes. We also added a short tolerance for the OTP flow so users with valid one-time codes won't get bounced if the cookie is dropped.

Please try the following (one at a time):
1) Clear cookies for zip.vendor-portal.com, open an incognito window and paste this link: https://zip.vendor-portal.com/invite/abc123?forceAccept=1
2) If that still loops, forward the exact time (including timezone) you attempt the acceptance and attach a short screen recording — we can match it with our logs.

If you want to avoid the portal entirely for now, we can send a direct activation email (one-click) that will complete setup and let you set the PO billing details afterwards.

Apologies again; we know this blocks POs. Once you confirm success I'll close SUP-5471 and share a short postmortem with the change and remediation steps for your IT team.
